sections.label: FAS 2034 World Cup goal
sections.summary: Speaker asks whether the Government plans to support FAS in its goal of reaching the 2034 World Cup and how success will be measured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: My heart, therefore, skipped a beat when I read of FAS’ announcement of its goal to get our national team to qualify for the 2034 World Cup.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: But I had mixed feelings about the announcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We are currently ranked 158th in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This will be a goal that will require not only the efforts of the FAS or our local football fraternity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I, therefore, invite the Minister to share with us whether the Government has plans to support the FAS in achieving this goal and, in so doing, how do we intend to measure our level of success?

sections.label: Safeguarding athletes from harassment
sections.summary: Speaker invites the Minister to share what the Ministry is doing to ensure a safe environment for athletes and guard against harassment and abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: However, more should and can always be done to safeguard our athletes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I, therefore, also invite the Minister to share more of what the Ministry is working towards to ensure that there is a safe and positive environment for our athletes to thrive and safeguard against harassment and abuse in the sports fraternity.

sections.label: Businesses on automation and workforce
sections.summary: Half of surveyed businesses plan to accelerate automation, 43% plan to reduce workforce and 34% plan to expand it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Half of businesses surveyed say they plan to accelerate the automation of jobs in their companies. 43% indicated that they plan to reduce their workforce due to technology integration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: On the other hand, 34% are planning to expand their workforce.

sections.label: SGTeguhBersatu taskforce established
sections.summary: Mr Masagos, with Malay ministers and MPs, established and led a taskforce called SGTeguhBersatu early last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   Early last year, the Minister-in-Charge of Muslim Affairs, Mr Masagos, together with the Malay ministers and MPs, established and led a taskforce called SGTeguhBersatu.

sections.label: Asatizah graduates taking other jobs
sections.summary: Speaker asks how many asatizah returning each year after graduation choose jobs other than becoming religious teachers or similar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How many asatizah who return every year after graduation are choosing and getting jobs other than becoming religious teachers or something similar?

sections.label: Equipping asatizah for social support
sections.summary: Speaker asks what is done to equip asatizah for social support, whether they attend counselling or pastoral care training, and how PCICS prepares them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Here I would like to ask what is being done to ensure that our asatizah are sufficiently equipped to provide social support to the community?

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Are they attending training or courses such as counselling or pastoral care?

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Announcements have also been made on the Postgraduate Certificate in Islam in Contemporary Societies (PCICS) scheduled to commence in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: How is this programme designed to prepare the asatizah to guide the Muslim community in Singapore in the face of new challenges?

sections.label: Committee on Future Asatizah convened
sections.summary: The Committee on Future Asatizah was convened in March 2019 to develop a vision for asatizah of the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Committee on Future Asatizah (COFA) was convened in March 2019 to develop a vision for asatizah of the future.

sections.label: Teen detained under ISA
sections.summary: In January this year, a 16-year-old Singaporean student was detained under the Internal Security Act for planning to attack two mosques and kill congregants on March 15.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   In January this year, a 16-year-old Singaporean student was detained under the Internal Security Act (ISA) for planning to attack two mosques and kill congregants in Singapore on March 15 this year – the second anniversary of the Christchurch terror attacks.

sections.label: Christchurch mosque shooter attack
sections.summary: The white supremacist, then 28 years old, stormed the Al Noor mosque with semi-automatic guns and shot Muslims at Friday prayers, killing 44 people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The white supremacist, then 28 years old, stormed the Al Noor mosque armed with semi-automatic guns and shot at Muslims gathered there for Friday prayers, killing 44 people.

sections.label: Muis interfaith understanding question
sections.summary: A question asks how Muis is working with other religious organisations to promote interfaith understanding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Could the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs share how Muis is working with other religious organisations to promote interfaith understanding?

sections.label: Community complaints on unanswered issues
sections.summary: Some community members and asatizah complained that no clear answers come from authorities on deviant teachings, halal certification management, and governance and financial management involving Madrasah Irsyad Zuhri Al-Islamiah.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It just that lately, some members of the community and our asatizah have complained that when crucial issues are voiced out or problems are raised, there are no clear answers from the authorities responsible for managing our welfare, needs and well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These issues that will be raised are, first of all, deviant teachings; second, the halal certification management; and thirdly, the issues of governance and financial management involving Madrasah Irsyad Zuhri Al-Islamiah Sir, in November last year, the Straits Times published a report on deviant teaching involving a man who has a number of wives.

sections.label: Muis reports matter to CPIB
sections.summary: MUIS said that it has reported this matter to the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau (CPIB).

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MUIS said that it has reported this matter to the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau (CPIB).

sections.label: MUIS halal certificate investigation findings
sections.summary: MUIS completed its investigation and announced findings on 15 December 2020, and two weeks later a report came from Malaysia about a halal meat certificate scandal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Subsequently, MUIS completed its investigation and announced its findings on 15 December 2020, but two weeks later on 29 December 2020, there was a report from across the Causeway about the halal meat certificate scandal in Malaysia.

sections.label: Questions on MUIS halal certification
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs what efforts MUIS took to refute Datuk Dr Sirajuddin's statement, which could affect trust in halal certification here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   My questions for the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs are as follows: What efforts or actions have MUIS taken to refute the statement by Datuk Dr Sirajuddin, which sounds worryingly like an accusation, and could affect Muslims' trust in the halal certification process here?

sections.label: M3 youth mentoring programmes
sections.summary: The Ministry, through M3, has taken steps to grow a mentoring culture for Malay/Muslim youths, with programmes like EPB, EPG, Project SOAR and a Youth Mentoring Office.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For the Malay/Muslim community, the Ministry has taken steps, through M3, to grow a strong culture of mentoring for its youths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have gender-specific programmes such as the Empowerment Programme for Boys (EPB) and the ITE Empowerment Programme for Girls (EPG) in the ITE, as well as Project SOAR, a community mentoring programme for secondary school students.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A Youth Mentoring Office has also been set up to train volunteers in becoming mentors and many programmes have been started.

sections.label: M3 support for at-risk youths
sections.summary: Through M3, MENDAKI, MUIS and MESRA strengths are leveraged to address at-risk youths' secular and religious growth and provide resources and referral mechanisms for their well-being.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Through M3, the different strengths of MENDAKI, MUIS and MESRA can be leveraged to address both the secular and religious growth of these at-risk youths, and provide the necessary resources and referral mechanisms to support their mental and emotional well-being.

sections.label: KMM programme beneficiaries
sections.summary: The question asks how many have benefited from the KMM programme in the three years since KMM was established.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the three years since the establishment of KMM, how many have benefited from the KMM programme?

sections.label: Engaging at-risk Malay/Muslim groups
sections.summary: Some families remain unaware of available programmes and support, and the question asks how the M3 network can more effectively engage at-risk groups in the Malay/Muslim community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, some families remain unaware of programmes, assistance and support that are available, and how to access them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I am concerned and would like to know, how we can, through the M3 network, engage at-risk groups within the Malay/Muslim community more effectively?

sections.label: Malay/Muslim workers digital green skills
sections.summary: An MP asks what more can be done through the M3 network, particularly MENDAKI SENSE, for Malay/Muslim workers to develop digital and green economy competencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Through the M3 network, in particular MENDAKI SENSE, may I ask the Minister, what more can we do for Malay/Muslim workers to develop their digital competencies or expertise in the green economy, so that they can be part of these emerging industries?

sections.label: MENDAKI youth mentoring programmes
sections.summary: MENDAKI has run youth mentoring programmes under its Youth Mentoring Office since last year, with over 1000 volunteers registered and over 500 trained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For younger students, MENDAKI has rolled out mentoring programmes for youth under the Youth Mentoring Office since last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: More than 1000 volunteers have registered as mentors and more than 500 mentors have been trained.

sections.label: Bersamamu programme couple participation
sections.summary: As of September last year, more than 5,700 couples had joined the Bersamamu programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   As of September last year, more than 5,700 couples have joined the Bersamamu programme.

sections.label: Malay participation in engagement sessions
sections.summary: MCCY held Emerging Stronger Together and Ciptasama sessions for the Malay/Muslim community, but only 6% of participants were Malay.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, MCCY had organised "Emerging Stronger Together" and "Ciptasama" sessions for the Malay/Muslim community to share their views and suggestions in building a community of success and a better Singapore for the future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I note from the "Emerging Stronger" website that only 6% of the participants in these conversations were Malay.

sections.label: M3@Towns network expansion
sections.summary: The M3@Towns network was expanded with the recently launched M3@Geylang Serai and M3@Jalan Besar.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: During this time, we have also expanded the M3@Towns network with the recently launched M3@Geylang Serai and M3@Jalan Besar.

sections.label: Low-income Malay social mobility
sections.summary: Middle- and high-income Malays have enjoyed good income growth, but relative social mobility remains a real struggle for some low-income Malays.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our middle- and high-income Malays have enjoyed good income growth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, for some low-income Malays, relative social mobility (in other words, those who were initially at the bottom of the socio-economic spectrum, and successfully climbed the ladder of success and reached the top) is a real struggle.

sections.label: M3 expansion to towns
sections.summary: Minister Maliki announced M3 has expanded to Geylang Serai, Jalan Besar and Toa Payoh.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   Minister Maliki recently announced that M³ has expanded to three other towns at Geylang Serai, Jalan Besar and Toa Payoh.

sections.label: IB students exam results
sections.summary: All 25 IB students passed, with an average score above the global average.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: All 25 students in the IB programme passed the exams, and their average score is higher than the average global scores.

sections.label: Madrasah curriculum beyond religious sector
sections.summary: The question asks if the Minister has plans to value-add the madrasah curriculum for experience beyond the religious sector.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share any plans to further value-add the madrasah curriculum in creating opportunities for madrasah students to gain experience beyond the religious sector?

sections.label: Ramadan SGUnited Buka Puasa initiative
sections.summary: During Ramadan, MUIS and community bodies launched the SGUnited Buka Puasa initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Throughout Ramadan last year, MUIS worked with community bodies such as the Singapore Malay Chamber of Commerce and Industry and Roses of Peace, among others, to launch the SGUnited Buka Puasa (Breaking of Fast) initiative.

sections.label: Online donations and zakat collection
sections.summary: OurMasjid.SG collected over three million dollars since April 2020, and zakat collection did not drop last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In the midst of COVID-19, digital adoption has become more prevalent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This includes the online donation portal, OurMasjid.SG, which has helped to provide continued funding support with more than three million dollars collected since it was launched in April 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that there was no reduction in zakat collected last year, despite the pandemic.

sections.label: Mufti irsyad on vaccines
sections.summary: The Office of the Mufti issued an irsyad that scientifically and medically safe and effective vaccines can be used by Muslims.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: When the COVID-19 vaccine became available, the Office of the Mufti quickly issued an irsyad that vaccines that are scientifically and medically safe and effective, and can be used by Muslims as this would save lives.

sections.label: MUIS PCICS programme commenced
sections.summary: MUIS successfully commenced the Postgraduate Certificate in Islam in Contemporary Society programme last April.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In this regard, MUIS successfully commenced the Postgraduate Certificate in Islam in Contemporary Society (PCICS) programme last April.

sections.label: Asatizah Workforce Development Plan
sections.summary: Last year, MUIS announced the Asatizah Workforce Development Plan to enhance career pathways and opportunities for asatizah.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Last year, MUIS announced the Asatizah Workforce Development Plan or AWDP which aims to enhance career pathways and opportunities for our asatizah.

sections.label: MSF Cinta Abadi rebate
sections.summary: MSF will provide a $70 rebate for couples attending the Cinta Abadi marriage preparation course from the second quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: MSF will also provide a $70 rebate for couples attending the "Cinta Abadi" marriage preparation course from the second quarter of this year.

sections.label: Engagements on women's development
sections.summary: Several engagements with the Malay/Muslim community on women's development will be led by Parliamentary Secretary Ms Rahayu Mahzam throughout this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To Ms Nadia's query, several engagements with our Malay/Muslim community on women’s development will be led by Parliamentary Secretary Ms Rahayu Mahzam throughout this year.

sections.label: Public Service uniform policy and tudungs
sections.summary: The Public Service uniform policy cannot be tilted towards any religious belief, and allowing tudungs would introduce a visible religious marker.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Save for the practices that we inherited as a legacy from the British government, our uniform policy in the Public Service cannot be tilted towards any religious belief, any particular religious belief.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Allowing tudungs would introduce a very visible religious marker that identify every tudung-wearing female nurse or uniformed officer as a Muslim.

sections.label: Closed-door discussions on tudung
sections.summary: After discussing with PAP Members of Parliament, the Government agreed to careful, closed-door discussions on sensitive issues like wearing tudung in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Race and religion will become increasingly polarising and this will harm all of us, especially the minority communities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Hence, after discussing the Government's considerations with the PAP Members of Parliament, we agreed to take the approach of careful, close-door discussions because we understand this complexity and sensitivity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: For sensitive issues like the wearing of tudung in the workplace, where uniforms are required, we continue to have discussions and consultations with the community, our community, especially, behind closed doors.

sections.label: Azan adjustments for non-Muslims
sections.summary: Adjustments were made for non-Muslims near mosques, including lowering the azan volume and playing it inwards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: On our part, we have made some adjustments in consideration to non-Muslims living near the mosques, such as lowering the volume of the azan and playing it inwards in the mosque.

sections.label: Community solidarity after mosque plot
sections.summary: After news of a 16-year-old Singaporean's detention for planning attacks on two mosques, the community showed solidarity and social cohesion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Recently, when news broke of the detention of the 16-year-old Singaporean who planned to conduct terrorist attacks against Muslims at two mosques, our community showed solidarity and social cohesion.

sections.label: Asatizah, MUIS interfaith efforts and M³
sections.summary: Asatizah and MUIS must strengthen interfaith understanding, and M³ was formed in 2018 to harness collaboration among MUIS, MENDAKI and MESRA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To Mr Fahmi Aliman's query, our asatizah and MUIS must continue to strengthen efforts to promote interfaith understanding – through religious teachings and guidance, and holding dialogues with other interfaith groups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, while the past year was full of unprecedented challenges, I am certain that as long as we continue to invest in the three key attributes – Competence, Character and Citizenry, we will emerge stronger from this crisis as a Community of Success, contributing to the success of our nation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, we formed M³ in 2018 to harness collaboration and tap on the combined resources, networks and expertise of MUIS, MENDAKI and MESRA as we strengthen the last-mile outreach and assistance to the community.

sections.label: Divorces in community increased
sections.summary: Divorces in the community increased by more than 12% over the last 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In general, divorces in our community has increased by more than 12% in the last 10 years.

sections.label: Support for inmates and families
sections.summary: They currently support close to 80 inmates, ex-inmates, and their families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Currently, they support close to 80 inmates, ex-inmates, and their families.

sections.label: Digital Access programme beneficiaries
sections.summary: Over 7,600 individuals benefited last year from IMDA's Digital Access programmes, which equipped low-income families, including students, with digital devices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Last year, over 7,600 individuals benefited from the Digital Access programmes by the Infocomm and Media Development Authority (IMDA), which equipped low-income families, including students, with digital devices.

sections.label: M³ Engagement Coordination Office setup
sections.summary: An M³ Engagement Coordination Office will be set up this year to coordinate outreach with Government programmes and Malay/Muslim organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Ms Mariam Jaafar and Ms Nadia asked how M³ and other Malay/Muslim organisations can work together with the Government to support the community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that we will be setting up the M³ Engagement Coordination Office, or ECO, this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: ECO will coordinate and strengthen outreach efforts with other Government programmes such as UPLIFT and ComLink, and various efforts by other Malay/Muslim organisations (MMO).

sections.label: ECO volunteer training framework
sections.summary: ECO will establish a training framework to equip volunteers with skills and understanding of national policies and Government schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: ECO will put in place a training framework for our volunteers, to equip them with the necessary skills, as well as deepen their understanding of national policies and Government schemes, that are especially useful for these vulnerable families.

sections.label: Volunteer and professional numbers
sections.summary: There are over 500 volunteers to date, including 150 professionals from the legal, education, and healthcare sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To date, we have over 500 volunteers, with 150 professionals from the legal, education, and healthcare sectors joining us.

sections.label: Kelas Siap Sekolah pilot launch
sections.summary: In May this year, MENDAKI will launch a new pilot programme, Kelas Siap Sekolah, to complement KMM@CC.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In May this year, MENDAKI will launch a new pilot programme called Kelas Siap Sekolah (KSS) to complement KMM@CC.

sections.label: KMM and eKMM beneficiaries
sections.summary: In total, 2,200 parents and children have benefited from KMM and eKMM.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In total, 2,200 parents and children have benefited from KMM and eKMM.

sections.label: MENDAKI SENSE jobseeker assistance
sections.summary: Since January 2020, MENDAKI SENSE has assisted over 4,000 jobseekers, with over 800 placed in jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Since January 2020, MENDAKI SENSE has assisted more than 4,000 jobseekers, with over 800 of them, successfully placed in jobs.

sections.label: MENDAKI SENSE digital training places
sections.summary: Since August 2020, MENDAKI SENSE has offered around 200 training places monthly in digital-related fields.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Since August 2020, MENDAKI SENSE has offered around 200 training places every month in digital-related fields.

sections.label: Malay WSQ courses and green economy
sections.summary: MENDAKI SENSE is identifying WSQ-certifiable courses conductable in Malay and will hold a green economy sharing session in Q2 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: MENDAKI SENSE is also currently identifying courses that are certifiable under WSQ that can be conducted in Malay.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: On employment and upskilling opportunities presented by the green economy, SENSE will conduct a sharing session in the second quarter of 2021.

sections.label: YMO mentoring and 2021 recruitment
sections.summary: Over 600 trained and over 500 deployed; this year MENDAKI aims to recruit 850 more mentors for 1,700 students in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Over 600 of them have been trained and over 500 deployed to programmes, such as MENDAKI Empowerment for ITE Boys and Girls and Project SOAR.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This would not have been possible without Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu Mahzam's tireless efforts in guiding the establishment of the YMO and in engaging the youths to build up a culture of mentorship in our community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This year, we aim to ramp up MENDAKI's mentoring programmes under YMO by recruiting an additional 850 mentors to mentor 1,700 students in the MENDAKI Tuition Scheme and Empowerment Programmes in 2021.

sections.label: MUIS complaints on deviant teaching
sections.summary: MUIS has received 32 complaints on potential deviant teaching and five reports on dubious religious teachings since 1968.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In response to Mr Faisal Manap's query, MUIS has received 32 complaints on potential deviant teaching, five reports on dubious religious teachings and practices since formation in 1968.

sections.label: MUIS refers matter to CPIB
sections.summary: MUIS referred the matter to CPIB and Police for investigation though it found no evidence of improper conduct by its officer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: MUIS has been open and transparent in referring the matter to the CPIB and Police for further investigations even as it found no evidence to support the allegations of improper conduct or abuse of power by its officer in handling the FHCB cases.

sections.label: MUIS wrote to JAKIM
sections.summary: After his statement, MUIS wrote to JAKIM in December 2020 to clarify the statement but has not heard back.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In fact, after his statement was made, MUIS immediately wrote to JAKIM officially in December 2020 to clarify that statement made but we have not heard from JAKIM on this matter.

sections.label: Madrasah Irsyad and Irsyad Trust
sections.summary: Madrasah Irsyad and Irsyad Trust Limited are currently not affiliated, and the Trust is an independent entity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: From what I understand though, Madrasah Irsyad and Irsyad Trust Limited are at present not affiliated, and the latter is an independent entity.

sections.label: Closed-door discussion with Faisal Manap
sections.summary: A closed-door discussion was held about why the issue was raised as it was and why it should not be public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: On the issue of consulting and talking to Mr Faisal Manap, I think he will recall that immediately after our last exchange, maybe about five years ago, we had a closed door discussion why I had to raise it the way I did it and what the points were and why we should not put this out in the open.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We had that closed-door discussion although it was not something that I invited him to, but I used that opportunity to explain to him behind closed doors, why this has to be done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: But it continues to be put out in the open – on every occasion that can be done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: And like I said, these are issues that we have our approach, which is to do it behind closed doors, with our leaders, who we hope can understand and know how to bring this up to the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: I know the Member continues to have a different approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: But may I also ask Dr Maliki to clarify on the issue of how to approach this so that this is not a closed door issue about how to approach on issues like this which are sensitive and complex?

sections.label: Engagement on Muslim women nurses
sections.summary: The matter is taken seriously, with continued engagement of union leaders, religious teachers and community members on the concerns.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: I want to assure our community and our Muslim women nurses that we take this matter very, very seriously.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: We have continued to engage union leaders, religious teachers, respected members of the community, putting to them the concerns of the Government, the other community leaders, as well as not just the Muslim community.

sections.label: Grand Imam on tudung at work
sections.summary: The Grand Imam advised Muslim women not to leave jobs solely over the tudung, citing a legal maxim permitting removal for work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: In response to a question on the tudung not being allowed in certain workplaces, the Grand Imam made it clear that while Islam commands women to wear the tudung, he advised Muslim women against leaving their jobs solely because they are not able to wear it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: He advised not to make the hijab an issue that determines your life to the extent that you have no choice but to leave your job; and he emphasised that there is a legal maxim in Islam that would permit Muslim women to take off their tudung due to work requirements.

sections.label: PAP Muslim MPs engaging communities
sections.summary: PAP Muslim Members of Parliament have continuously engaged the Government and various communities to find a way forward for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: We have seen it happen and we must guard against it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: That is why the PAP Muslim Members of Parliament have continuously been engaging the Government and the various communities, not just the Malay community or Muslim community, in order find a way forward for the greater good of Singapore and Singaporeans.

sections.label: Keeping racial and religious harmony
sections.summary: The speaker hopes Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap understands this cannot be taken for granted and ensures Singapore's harmony.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: I sincerely hope that Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap understands that too.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: This is something we cannot take for granted.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: This is something that will ensure Singapore's racial and religious harmony continues to be kept the way it is.

sections.label: Kelas Siap Sekolah programme
sections.summary: Kelas Siap Sekolah is a new programme continuing KMM@CC, with two runs from May to October 2021 and about 100 kids in the pilot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: To answer the Member's question, Kelas Siap Sekolah is a new programme that we are putting in place as a continuation for our KMM@CC programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: A few things that we want to go for: to nurture them with literacy and arithmetic skills in one setting and to also improve their love for learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We are going to have two runs from May to October 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Each run will be held over eight sessions, including the post-programme assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We hope to have about 100 kids benefit from the pilot programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As of December 2020, the MMPG has now 80 children from 53 families enrolled.

sections.label: PA operating expenditure comparison
sections.summary: PA's FY2021 operating expenditure is $589 million with 2,565 staff, and in FY2020 it spent 30% on activities and 70% on administration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Furthermore, from actual expenditures of FY2020, PA has spent only $199 million, which is about 30% of its running cost on activities and projects, with the balance of $441 million, which is 70% of its running cost, spent on administration.

sections.label: PA role and political party members
sections.summary: The passage asks whether PA's role can be redefined and seeks the proportion of PA's leaders, staff and volunteers who are members of any political party.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, is there more that we can do to redefine the role of PA at the higher level and to to ensure that the funds are deployed in areas that help our needy Singaporeans most?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We would like to know the proportion of PA’s leaders, staff and volunteers who are members of any political party.

sections.label: Churches reach out to mosque

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: A few churches in my constituency reached out to the Masjid Jamek Queenstown, also in my division, for a sharing and meal together as an expression of solidarity, to deepen the ties between both faiths and condemned the incident.

sections.label: MCCY religious tolerance initiatives

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I commend MCCY for its work to build up religious tolerance among our people and look forward to hearing its new initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I propose MCCY facilitating regular sharing sessions among our different faiths which is key to building trust and understanding.

sections.label: MCCY encouraging volunteers and corporates
sections.summary: The passage asks how MCCY is encouraging individuals, including youths, and corporates to volunteer and contribute.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: How is MCCY encouraging more individuals from all walks of life, including youths, as well as corporates, to step forward, volunteer and contribute to make a positive impact?

sections.label: Self-radicalised Christian boy's mosque attack plan
sections.summary: A self-radicalised Christian boy planned terrorist-style attacks on two mosques in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The case of the self-radicalised Christian boy who was planning terrorist-style attacks on two mosques here is a case in point.

sections.label: Racial slurs over native-born status
sections.summary: An ugly episode of racial slurs and comments followed about whether he was a native-born Singapore Son.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: What followed, however, was an ugly episode of racial slurs and comments whether he was a native-born Singapore Son or not.

sections.label: Students' volunteering and CCA ideas
sections.summary: Students suggested schools inform them of volunteering opportunities, encourage long-term volunteer work, and fund inter-school CCAs in niche activities.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Some ideas from students are: (a) have schools inform students regularly of volunteering opportunities outside of schools; (b) encourage more long-term volunteer work such as solving community problems together so that they can work on a project for a longer period and have longer interactions; (c) provide more funding for inter-school CCAs in niche activities such as board games, fashion design, cultural and sports events.

sections.label: Educating new citizens on social norms
sections.summary: New citizens, PRs and work pass holders should be educated on social norms to respect Singapore's multi-racial, multi-religious and multicultural aspects.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: New citizens, PRs and work pass holders should be educated on our social norms so that they can respect the multi-racial, multi-religious and multicultural aspects of our home.

sections.label: Arts and culture hit by COVID-19
sections.summary: The arts and culture industry is among the hardest hit by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The arts and culture industry is amongst the hardest hit by COVID-19.

sections.label: Digital needs of artists and creatives
sections.summary: Artists need a digital stage, but tech resources are scarce and funding is needed, especially for gig workers, SEPs and SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To go digital, artists need a digital stage but tech resources are scarce and funding is needed, especially since many in the creative sector are gig workers, self-employed professionals (SEPs) and SMEs.

sections.label: Arts resilience package and gig workers
sections.summary: Performances have returned with 250-person audience limits and bubble wrap seating, and the question asks whether the $45 million Resilience Package supports gig workers and SEPs in creative industries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Performances have started to come back but audience max at 250 people and in "bubble wrap seating".

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Does the $45 million Resilience Package, which is much appreciated, support the gig workers and SEPs in our creative industries?

sections.label: Arts practitioners moving to other industries
sections.summary: The passage lists COVID-19 initiatives and asks whether the Ministry knows how many arts practitioners, technicians and freelancers have moved to other industries.

sentences.text: To copy with COVID-19, the Government has provided initiatives like the Arts and Culture Resilience Package, the Jobs Support Scheme for employees and for freelancers, the Self-employed Persons Income Relief Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, the curbs on earning income have led to arts practitioners taking on other gigs such as becoming Grab drivers in order to pay bills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I wonder if the Ministry has an idea of the number of arts practitioners, technicians and other freelancers who have moved on to other industries, perhaps, never to return.

sections.label: Review of live performance rules
sections.summary: The passage asks whether, given arguably lower risks, there is room to review the rules around live performances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given the arguably lower risks, is there room for a review of the rules around live performances?

sections.label: Arts buy-in and COVID-19 recovery
sections.summary: The passage asks how successful the Government has been in getting arts industry buy-in on urban governance plans and asks MCCY to elaborate on its COVID-19 recovery plan for the Arts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How successful has the Government been in getting buy-in from the arts industry regarding their urban governance plans?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And finally, could the MCCY elaborate on its COVID-19 recovery plan for the Arts?

sections.label: Arts and sports support measures
sections.summary: The passage states MCCY introduced support measures including the Arts and Culture Resilience Package with operating grants up to $75,000 for over 300 organisations and the sports Resilience Package, and that both would be extended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: Last year, MCCY introduced a broad range of support measures for the arts and culture and sports fraternities, for example, the Arts and Culture Resilience Package includes an operating grant of up to $75,000 for over 300 eligible organisations, whereas the sports Resilience Package supports critical players and preserves core capabilities and pipeline development in our eco-system through operating grants and allowances for coaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: I am glad that both packages would be extended in this year's Budget.

sections.summary: The passage asks MCCY for plans to enhance participation in arts, culture and sports, and for updates on Team Singapore's preparations and athletes' safety for the Tokyo, Hanoi and Para Games.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: Can MCCY update on Team Singapore's preparation for the Tokyo Olympic and Paralympics, and Hanoi's SEA Games and Para Games, and how can we ensure athletes' safety and well-being amidst travelling and training?

sections.label: Athletes training and Goal 2034
sections.summary: Athletes must train and qualify, and agencies should give eligible athletes opportunities and resources; Goal 2034 was mooted by FAS in 2019 and discussed in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: Our athletes will still need to train and qualify for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: I hope that the respective Government agencies will provide adequate opportunities and access to resources, for eligible athletes to train and prepare themselves adequately for the glory of Singapore. "Goal 2034" was an idea mooted by FAS in August 2019 and discussed at the 2020 COS debates.

sections.label: Irfan Fandi wins Thai league
sections.summary: Irfan Fandi, with his club BG Pathum, became the first Singaporean in a team that won Thailand's top tier football league.

sentences.text: Last week, Irfan Fandi as part of his club BG Pathum, became the first Singaporean to be part of a team that won Thailand’s top tier football league.

sections.label: 2034 and primary school students

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: We must act swiftly before this window of opportunity narrows.

sections.label: Hawker culture added to UNESCO list
sections.summary: Hawker centres reflect migrant heritage, and hawker culture was officially added to the UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hawker centres are a symbol of our rich migrant heritage, harking back to a time when itinerant hawkers plied the streets to cook up instant meals of comfort food from their own unique cultures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It was thus truly a historic moment for us when our hawker culture was recently officially added to the UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity; this only further reinforced the fact that our hawker centres and hawker culture are truly a part of our home and heritage.

sections.label: Singaporeans value hawker centres
sections.summary: Nine out of 10 Singaporeans strongly feel hawker centres are integral to national culture and voted to preserve this culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Nine out of 10 Singaporeans strongly feel that the hawker centres are an integral part of our national culture and have voted in favour of preserving this culture.

sections.label: Ci Yuan hawker centre social enterprise
sections.summary: The Ci Yuan Community Club hawker centre was the first of 20 new hawker centres built over 12 years and used a social enterprise model.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The hawker centre in Ci Yuan Community Club in my Constituency was part of the Government's efforts to keep the cost of eating out affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It was the first of 20 new hawker centres to be built over a 12-year period and employed a social enterprise model to encourage more people to take up the hawker profession.

sections.label: Sustaining spirit of care

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: How will MCCY sustain this spirit of care?

sentences.text: To cite one example, the Inter-Racial and Religious Confidence Circles worked with the Singapore Malay Chamber of Commerce and Industry to distribute more than 18,000 Hari Raya cookies to 16 community isolation facilities for migrant workers.

sections.label: Emerging Stronger Conversations report

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In February 2021, we published the Singapore Together Emerging Stronger Conversations (ESCs) report.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: MCCY will set up two SG Together AfAs, bringing the total to 18.

sections.label: Resilience packages enhanced

sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced during the Budget that the Arts and Culture Resilience Package (ACRP) and Sport Resilience Package (SRP) will be enhanced.

sentences.text: Over 100 charities have benefited from it between 2014 and 2019, with close to $265 million matched.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Therefore, a Safe Sport Programme will be established through the Safe Sport Commission.

sections.label: Istana Main Building restoration

sentences.text: About 1,400 youths will be engaged through the Youth Corps Leaders Programme and Programme X in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)

sections.label: Investing in arts and culture

sentences.text: Through this sharing, I hope to take this opportunity to urge the Government – while dealing with challenges brought about by COVID-19 on the economic livelihood and social front, spare some thought on investing more in the development of arts and culture, especially the Chinese arts and culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The Government can introduce more effective incentives to support our young aspiring arts practitioners to create and voice their views.

sections.label: Support measures for arts sector

sentences.text: The Government's broad-based support measures and the Arts and Culture Resilience Package would have helped to provide some buoyancy but it remained challenging.

sentences.text: In this regard, I applaud the launch of the #SGCultureAnywhere campaign by the National Arts Council, as it offers a platform for practitioners to make their work a lot more accessible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Also, how does the Ministry intend to support the sector to adopt more digital solutions and experiment to create digital arts and culture products that can be scaled to reach a wider audience?

sections.label: Boosting arts and culture exposure

sentences.text: Chairman, there is a need to boost the exposure of arts and culture to help nurture Singaporeans to enhance their expression, creativity and shape individual and collective personality.
